requirements.requirement: Run the inventory web application on node2, listening on port 8080.
requirements.summary: node2 directly showed a running, boot-enabled service listening on 0.0.0.0:8080 and returning healthy inventory HTML and API responses, including after restart.

requirements.requirement: Run the inventory web application on node3, listening on port 8080.
requirements.summary: node3 directly showed a running, boot-enabled service listening on 0.0.0.0:8080 and returning healthy inventory HTML and API responses, including after restart.

requirements.requirement: Configure node1 to accept HTTP on port 80 and load-balance requests across node2 and node3.
requirements.summary: node1 directly showed a running, boot-enabled port-80 listener. Six successive requests alternated between node2 and node3, and final checks showed both backends healthy. Traffic also continued through the surviving backend during each backend restart and returned to alternating behavior afterward.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: All nodes remained on CentOS 5.11 with kernel 2.6.18-398.el5. The implementation used the existing Python 2.4.3 runtime, and the before/after lifecycle observations confirm unchanged kernel versions.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct functional evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed on every node: each had a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data state; node1 recovered access to both backends, while node2 and node3 recovered load-balancer membership. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently match the observed transitions.
limitations: The lifecycle listening-socket snapshots were empty even though nearby direct netstat checks showed the required listeners, so socket state relies on the executor's direct checks.

Systemd failed-service collection was unsupported on this legacy platform, and the lifecycle package-health command was incompatible with the installed yum version; independent hygiene coverage for failed services and package consistency is therefore limited.

operational_hygiene.summary: Task-related service files, SysV enablement, narrowly scoped backend firewall rules, the public port-80 rule, and required restarts all had clear roles. Minor retained residue remained: node1's bounded load-balancer verification left /tmp/lb-body, and each required reboot command left a /tmp/[REDACTED].log file. These artifacts were not cleaned up and remained after execution. No other unnecessary mutations were identified.
